cells.tense: Real weight is in your hands right now and it's steady — nobody has to stand over you to keep it moving.
cells.ask: Sit down and pick which of the things you're holding gets fed next — an hour or a small amount of money pointed at the one with the most room to grow, not the one that's loudest today.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day this looks like picking the load back up after a night's sleep and getting it to the end — the same person in the morning as the one who set it down. That's what holding firm is here, and the plain days are supposed to look like that.

What's in front of you is open ground, nothing committed yet, and the same strength that keeps the load moving is what picks the direction. So the next thing you pour energy into is a choice, not a sentence already written. Which one you feed next is still yours to say, and the strength you'd notice tomorrow is the one that gets built by continuing, not by squeezing harder.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived — reading tomorrow's difficulty today and tensing for it.
cells.ask: Count what you've done for someone this week and say one true word about what came back — once, out loud or in writing, before you do anything else for them.
cells.core:
When it's going well here, work gets done across days without anyone keeping score — you give, someone gives back, and neither side has to run the numbers. That's the ordinary shape of it, and it holds even when the work is heavy.

What's happening now is that holding firm is turning into anticipating. You're preparing for hardship that may not be yours, and the strain of it is real even though the load isn't here yet. The strength you have is for carrying what's actually in your hands, and bracing like this spends it on nothing. The give-and-take you already have is what tells you where you stop and someone else begins, and it's the only honest measure of how much is really yours to hold.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you — the strength held, and you've stayed back at the part that had no witness.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you carried through — a week when nothing was said about it, a job that got done with no one watching — in plain words, and let them hear the whole of it once.
cells.core:
On a good ordinary day, you carry what's in front of you and set it down when it's finished — the rest between one load and the next is part of the same strength, not a gap in it. That's what holding firm looks like when nothing gets stuck.

What's happening now is that the set-down got skipped. Something got carried through and nobody marked it, and you've kept holding past the end of the thing it was for. The strength isn't gone; it's still there in the private places you've been working from. What's missing is anyone hearing that it happened, and that's the smallest thing that puts the weight back in the ground it came from rather than on you.

cells.tense: You're holding things through and calling it just what has to be done — the strength is running, and you haven't taken it as yours.
cells.ask: Say one sentence about what you're carrying right now, in your own words, and do one next small thing toward it — the very next step, today, not the whole of it.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day, you try the thing that didn't work yesterday and don't count that as a loss — the trying is what keeps it alive. That's plain, and it's most of what holding firm is made of.

The strength you're using has no author in the story you tell. You call it getting through, or the situation, or what needed doing, and none of those say who did it. What's running is yours, and the way back is one step at a time: you name what you're carrying, in your own words, and keep going from there. What you keep doing is yours — say so once, and the next step starts counting as yours too.

attempts.check: The riskiest claim is that the person has already done the holding and knows it — statuses 3 and 4 both lean on a past the record doesn't contain, so I've kept it to a location (what was carried, in private) and left out what happened, who saw it, or what it cost. A reader might say the strain is just tiredness, not holding; the asks still work if that's true, because each one produces evidence either way — a rest taken, a no said, words written down, one more attempt made. The sentence I most had to talk myself out of was any line celebrating persistence as a virtue; that would serve the writer's cadence and leave the person with nothing to set down.
